action: Dorsata's notice recommends affected patients review account statements and credit reports closely and report suspicious activity or identity theft. General advice: Metabase users should apply the vendor's patch.
exec: A zero-day in analytics software used by many healthcare organisations exposed patient data at a health-technology vendor.
plain: An unauthorized party used a flaw in a data-reporting tool to reach health records of about 58,000 patients held by a US health-tech company, according to HIPAA Journal.

sources.name: Dorsata notice filed with the California Attorney General

summary: Dorsata's notice says a vulnerability in its Metabase business intelligence software allowed unauthorized access to its database platform from August 10 to 12, 2026; Social Security numbers were not involved. HIPAA Journal reports 58,249 individuals, patients of provider partners, with names, treatment and insurance details, and calls the flaw previously unknown (zero-day). It says VenariX saw Dire Wolf exploit it later.
title: Metabase zero-day exploited in Dorsata breach affecting 58,249 patients

validation.note: Two publishers state the breach: the Dorsata notice filed with the California Attorney General and HIPAA Journal. Primary: Dorsata's own notice letter on the California Attorney General's site (read 22 Nov) states Metabase's 12 August notice, the 10-12 August access window and that Social Security numbers were not involved; it gives no count and does not call the flaw a zero-day. The 58,249 count, data types and Dire Wolf link rest on HIPAA Journal. The notice's return address is Charlottesville, VA; HIPAA Journal gives Arlington, VA.

review.note: Action advice unsourced (now Dorsata's notice / General advice); 'a researcher' now VenariX per HIPAA Journal; data types 'may have included'; source published day and 58,249 evidence added; PDF notice read

date_note: Date of HIPAA Journal's report of the filing; the page gives no earlier disclosure day. Access was August 10-12.

evidence.quote: has recently disclosed a data breach to the HHS' Office for Civil Rights involving the protected health information of 58,249 individuals.
Our investigation determined the Metabase security vulnerability allowed unauthorized access to our database platform from August 10, 2026, to August 12, 2026.
